what_this_is: The raw MCP conversation with the ingredient-database server, captured without the SDK: plain JSON-RPC lines over stdin/stdout.
where_the_model_runs: Nowhere in this file. Every line below is the host asking the server for data and the server answering. The model is called only by the host (agent/agent.py) to decide WHICH of these calls to make; the server never calls a model and does not know one exists.
transport: stdio: the server is a child process; requests go to its stdin, replies come back on its stdout, one JSON object per line.

field_notes.capabilities: What each side supports: tools, resources, prompts, sampling.
field_notes.content: The tool's output, as a list of content blocks (usually one text block).
field_notes.id: Matches a reply to its request. Notifications have no id because nothing answers them.
field_notes.instructions: A short note from the server about what it is for. The host may show it to the model.
field_notes.isError: Set when the tool itself failed although the protocol worked. In our capture the failing call shows isError=false, because the tool chose to RETURN a description of the problem as ordinary data ("'unicorn tears' is not in the ingredient database", plus did_you_mean and next_step) instead of raising. That is the recoverable pattern: the model reads it and fixes its own call. An exception would have become a JSON-RPC error and ended the step.
field_notes.jsonrpc: Always "2.0". MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, an old and boring standard, which is the point.
field_notes.method: What is being asked for: initialize, tools/list, tools/call.
field_notes.protocolVersion: Which version of MCP both sides agree to speak.
field_notes.result: The server's answer. A reply has either result or error, never both.
field_notes.serverInfo: The server's own name and version, as it reports itself.
field_notes.tools: The discovered tool list. THIS is what makes a tool usable without writing any code: name, description and a JSON Schema for the arguments.

exchange.raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"resources":{"listChanged":false,"subscribe":false},"tools":{"listChanged":false}},"instructions":"Reference data about individual ingredients: weights, allergens, substitutes.","protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","serverInfo":{"name":"ingredient-db","version":"0.4.2"}}}

result.instructions: Reference data about individual ingredients: weights, allergens, substitutes.

exchange.raw:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"description":"Look up reference facts about a single ingredient: allergens and weight per cup.

Use this for questions about an ingredient itself rather than about a recipe, for
example "is tahini a nut?" or "what allergen is in buttermilk". For how much of an
ingredient a recipe needs, use the recipe tools instead.
","inputSchema":{"properties":{"name":{"title":"Name","type":"string"}},"required":["name"],"type":"object","title":"ingredient_infoArguments"},"name":"ingredient_info"},{"description":"Convert a weight of one ingredient into US cups, using that ingredient's density.

Flour and water weigh very different amounts per cup, so this needs the ingredient
name as well as the grams: grams_to_cups("strong white bread flour", 900).
","inputSchema":{"properties":{"name":{"title":"Name","type":"string"},"grams":{"title":"Grams","type":"number"}},"required":["name","grams"],"type":"object","title":"grams_to_cupsArguments"},"name":"grams_to_cups"},{"description":"List what an ingredient can be swapped for, with the ratio and the catch.

Use when the cook says they don't have something. Returns an empty list when the
database records no safe swap, which means "don't guess one".
","inputSchema":{"properties":{"name":{"title":"Name","type":"string"}},"required":["name"],"type":"object","title":"substitutes_forArguments"},"name":"substitutes_for"}]}}

tools.description:
Look up reference facts about a single ingredient: allergens and weight per cup.

Use this for questions about an ingredient itself rather than about a recipe, for
example "is tahini a nut?" or "what allergen is in buttermilk". For how much of an
ingredient a recipe needs, use the recipe tools instead.
tools.name: ingredient_info

tools.description:
Convert a weight of one ingredient into US cups, using that ingredient's density.

Flour and water weigh very different amounts per cup, so this needs the ingredient
name as well as the grams: grams_to_cups("strong white bread flour", 900).
tools.name: grams_to_cups

tools.description:
List what an ingredient can be swapped for, with the ratio and the catch.

Use when the cook says they don't have something. Returns an empty list when the
database records no safe swap, which means "don't guess one".
tools.name: substitutes_for
